readerQuestion: How can I make an existing Home Assistant roller shade lower when the sun reaches its window, while keeping manual control and avoiding needless motor movements?
directAnswer: Start with one position-controlled interior shade, observe its sun-angle range, add an explicit pause and rehearse the supplied notification-only rule. After verifying the decisions, replace its last action with set_cover_position. It only lowers, preserves a farther-closed position, and leaves reopening manual. Cloud behavior needs a separately observed brightness threshold.
originalContribution: Sections 2 and 4-6 provide an original native automation, west-window 230-310 degree example and north-wrap calculation, a seven-row decision table, harmless pause/preview tests, position tolerance, and an exact one-action transition to motor control. Published YAML was parsed and its templates checked against 25 synthetic cases including compass wrap, threshold equality, missing/invalid data, moving cover, pause, time limits and never requesting a more-open target. This was an offline PyYAML/Jinja evaluation with mocked entity functions, not a Home Assistant runtime test.
limitations: No shade, sensor, motor calibration, Home Assistant installation, energy savings or latency was tested. Angle, time, position and lux values are examples to verify in the room. A numeric position or brightness value can be stale/estimated; this routine cannot detect that. Requires working position control and reliable feedback; not for tilt-only devices, awnings, exit shutters or powered doors/windows. Reopening is manual. Local operation depends on the selected motor integration. Cover image is generated editorial illustration.
proofreadFixes: Final automated proofreading made three concrete corrections: bounded the configurable shade target to 0-100 and distinguished numeric position feedback from verified physical position; stated that re-enabling the toggle immediately checks conditions and may move the shade; and stated that the optional lux condition cannot detect a stale numeric reading. Confirmed the 35% value means open percentage, tilt is a separate action, a more-closed position remains untouched, the main YAML contains only a notification action, and all safety/pause/time checks are inside the action list. Verified old preview messages are explicitly labeled last qualifying decisions. Corrected the internal brief to describe the existing house-mode arrival/departure guidance accurately instead of claiming a zone.home code example. Final reread passed; no human or expert review claimed.

claimChecks.claim: Sun azimuth is clockwise from north and elevation is height above the horizon, calculated using the configured home location. Sun geometry does not itself observe shade obstructions or cloudy-day room brightness. Example angles are declared illustrative.
cover.set_cover_position targets 0 closed through100 open. The article uses an exact shade entity, bounds the chosen target, and compares reported position before sending a lower-only target.
Lift position and slat tilt are separate supported capabilities; tilt_position is not a replacement field in this lift-position example.

Cover position feedback may be absent, and SET_POSITION and SET_TILT_POSITION are separate features. This design requires position support and skips missing/non-numeric feedback; a plausible value still needs physical verification.
Time-pattern, Home Assistant start and state-change triggers can start the rule. The five-minute reevaluation reads the current state after startup and does not replay missed events.
An action-list condition stops subsequent actions when false, so paused, out-of-hours and invalid-data cases do not reach the notification or optional motor action.

Toggle helpers normally restore prior state; pausing this rule is distinct from stopping a motor, reopening the shade or pausing other controllers. Re-enabling triggers a new check because the example explicitly watches to:on.
The initial persistent notification appears inside Home Assistant; a reused notification_id updates one item. It is not a phone push alert and the published preview sends no cover command.

Run actions bypasses triggers and top-level conditions; the article retains checks inside actions and separately asks readers to inspect a scheduled trace. The first verification step leaves all motor commands absent.

The optional numeric-state condition requires a value strictly above the example threshold and does not pass unavailable/nonnumeric input. It does not detect stale numeric readings and cannot reopen the shade.
